$comment: THE PINNED SPECIFICATION for a card's identity. This file is the
contract between two independent implementations: card_identity.c,
which runs on the ATtiny1616 and writes the tag, and the host side in
pond/src/card/, which records the same card in cards.csv and verifies
If those two disagree by one bit of ordering, EVERY card is unknown to
the server at once - and it fails quietly, because an unknown serial is
designed to degrade rather than error. So neither side is tested
against the other. Both are tested against this file.
Never edit the vectors by hand - that would make this agree with

serial.input: SIGROW.SERNUM, all ten bytes, in the order the chip presents them
serial.serial_key_ascii_note: 15 characters; the 16th key byte is 0x00 - see serial_key_hex for the exact bytes
serial.bit_order: most significant group first, 5 bits per character
why_hashed_not_sliced: BUILD-PLAN originally said 'the low 40 bits' of SERNUM. SERNUM is lot
number, wafer number and die coordinates - a hundred cards from one
reel share a lot, so any fixed 40-bit slice is partly CONSTANT across
the batch. The '4 in a billion' collision estimate assumes 40 uniform
bits and would not have been true of the thing it described.
Hashing all ten bytes uses every bit of entropy the chip has and
makes that estimate honest. See the 'reel sibling' vectors below:
two chips one die coordinate apart produce unrelated serials.

token.purpose: the card SIGNS its claim - an unseen counter is not a credential
token.message: the 8 ASCII serial characters, then the counter as 2 bytes LITTLE-ENDIAN; 10 bytes, no separator, no NUL
token.test_key_is_not_the_real_secret: FIRMWARE_SECRET never enters this repository; see secrets.h.example

counter.rule: increment EEPROM FIRST, then write the NDEF - the other order lets a consumed counter reappear, which is the one outcome that breaks the scheme

url.digit_is_first: so the one byte the MCU patches per fortune never moves

serials.note: reel sibling B, one die coordinate away
